title: Minimal Polynomial of √2 + √3 + √5
description: Computes the candidate minimal polynomial of α = √2+√3+√5 over ℚ: p(X) = X⁸ − 40X⁶ + 352X⁴ − 960X² + 576, the Galois-conjugate product ∏_{ε∈{±1}³}(X − ε₁√2 − ε₂√3 − ε₃√5). Fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms): p annihilates α and all eight sign-conjugates via a single sign-independent 'isolate √2 and square' computation; p is monic of degree 8; α is integral over ℚ; and the genuine minimal polynomial divides p. The full identity minpoly ℚ α = p is given as a theorem with irreducibility as an explicit hypothesis (equivalently [ℚ(√2+√3+√5):ℚ]=8, the parent's oq-04 multiquadratic-degree question, not yet in Mathlib). The n=3 analogue of the sister entry sqrt2-plus-sqrt3-irrational-oq-03 (n=2, quartic X⁴−10X²+1).

meta.author: Lean Genius (researcher-3)
meta.assumptions: 0 sorries, 0 literal `axiom` declarations, no `native_decide` (so no `Lean.ofReduceBool`). Every theorem is fully machine-checked. The centerpiece identity minpoly ℚ (√2+√3+√5) = X⁸−40X⁶+352X⁴−960X²+576 is stated as `minpoly_eq_of_irreducible`, a genuine theorem that takes irreducibility of the octic over ℚ as an explicit hypothesis — this is NOT an axiom but a discharged-elsewhere assumption. Irreducibility is equivalent to [ℚ(√2+√3+√5):ℚ]=8 (the parent entry's open question oq-04), which requires multiquadratic field-degree machinery not present in Mathlib v4.26.0. The unconditional results (root witness for all 8 conjugates, monicity, degree 8, integrality, minpoly ∣ p) are assumption-free.
originalContributions: conjugates_are_roots: a single sign-independent computation proving that ALL EIGHT sign-conjugates ε₁√2+ε₂√3+ε₃√5 are roots of X⁸−40X⁶+352X⁴−960X²+576 (uses only a²=2, b²=3, c²=5, never the signs) — directly realizes the Galois-conjugate product structure
aeval_minpoly_candidate: √2+√3+√5 is a root of the explicit octic, proved via the chain ((α²−6−2√15)²=8α²) closed by one linear_combination
cand_monic / cand_natDegree: the octic is monic of degree 8 (monicity!, compute_degree!)
minpoly_eq_of_irreducible: conditional identity minpoly ℚ α = octic, with irreducibility as an explicit hypothesis

overview.historicalContext: For distinct primes $p_1,\dots,p_k$, the field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{p_1},\dots,\sqrt{p_k})$ is the multiquadratic extension of degree $2^k$, with Galois group $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^k$ acting by independent sign flips. A theorem going back to Besicovitch (1940) shows the $\sqrt{p_i}$ are $\mathbb{Q}$-linearly independent, and a classical primitive-element argument shows $\sqrt{p_1}+\dots+\sqrt{p_k}$ generates the whole field, hence has degree exactly $2^k$. For $k=3$ with $p_i \in \{2,3,5\}$ the minimal polynomial of $\sqrt2+\sqrt3+\sqrt5$ therefore has degree $8$, obtained as the product over the eight Galois conjugates $\prod_{\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}^3}(X-\varepsilon_1\sqrt2-\varepsilon_2\sqrt3-\varepsilon_3\sqrt5)$. Computing its coefficients (all even powers, since the conjugate set is closed under global sign flip) gives $X^8-40X^6+352X^4-960X^2+576$. As with the $k=2$ Klein-four case ($X^4-10X^2+1$), this octic factors modulo every prime yet is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$.
overview.problemStatement: Compute the minimal polynomial of α = √2 + √3 + √5 over ℚ (open question oq-03 of the parent entry): exhibit the explicit degree-8 polynomial and establish its defining properties via the Galois-conjugate product.
overview.text: We exhibit p(X) = X⁸ − 40X⁶ + 352X⁴ − 960X² + 576 and verify the structure that makes it the minimal polynomial. The root witness is proved by the classical isolate-and-square chain: with a=√2, b=√3, c=√5 and t=bc=√15, one has (a+b+c)² − 2a(a+b+c) = 6 + 2t (isolating √2), so ((a+b+c)²−6−2t)² = 8(a+b+c)²; a single linear_combination over this relation and t²=15 collapses to p(a+b+c)=0. Crucially the computation never uses the signs of a, b, c — only a²=2, b²=3, c²=5 — so the identical proof shows all eight sign-conjugates ε₁√2+ε₂√3+ε₃√5 are roots of p, which is exactly the Galois-conjugate family. We further prove p is monic of degree 8, that α is integral over ℚ, and that the genuine minimal polynomial divides p. The final identity minpoly ℚ α = p is provided as minpoly_eq_of_irreducible, taking irreducibility of p (equivalently [ℚ(α):ℚ]=8) as an explicit hypothesis: unlike the n=2 quartic — where a finite rational/quadratic-factor analysis settles irreducibility — the degree-8 case reduces to the multiquadratic field-degree fact (the parent's oq-04), which is beyond the current Mathlib API. We therefore do not over-claim a full verification of the equality.
overview.proofStrategy: Four parts: (I) conjugates_are_roots — a sign-independent isolate-and-square computation, closed by two linear_combinations, proving p vanishes on every ε₁√2+ε₂√3+ε₃√5. (II) aeval_minpoly_candidate — specialize to α=√2+√3+√5 after reducing aeval to the real computation via simp + Real.sq_sqrt. (III) cand_monic (monicity!), cand_natDegree (compute_degree!), sqrt_sum_isIntegral (the monic annihilator witnesses integrality). (IV) minpoly_dvd_cand (minpoly.dvd, always valid) and minpoly_eq_of_irreducible (minpoly.eq_of_irreducible_of_monic with irreducibility hypothesized).
keyInsights: Sign-independence is the whole point: because the isolate-and-square chain only ever uses a²=2, b²=3, c²=5 and never the signs of a, b, c, one proof simultaneously certifies all eight Galois conjugates as roots — the computational shadow of the conjugate product ∏_{ε∈{±1}³}(X−ε₁√2−ε₂√3−ε₃√5).

Why only even powers: the eight-element conjugate set is closed under the global sign flip ε ↦ −ε, so the roots pair up as ±r. Hence p(X)=p(−X) and all odd-degree coefficients vanish, leaving X⁸−40X⁶+352X⁴−960X²+576.

The coefficients (e₂,e₄,e₆,e₈)=(−40,352,−960,576) are the elementary symmetric functions of the eight roots; equivalently they follow from the power sums Σr²=80, Σr⁴=1792, Σr⁶=49280, Σr⁸=1412608 via Newton's identities (odd power sums vanish by the ± pairing).

The degree-8 obstruction: irreducibility over ℚ is equivalent to [ℚ(√2+√3+√5):ℚ]=8, i.e. the multiquadratic-degree fact. Mathlib v4.26.0 lacks the multi-quadratic API (it has cyclotomic and Kummer cases but not independent sign-flip automorphisms), so — unlike the n=2 quartic, whose irreducibility is a finite coefficient analysis — the full minpoly identity is left conditional rather than over-claimed.

Relation to the sister entry: sqrt2-plus-sqrt3-irrational-oq-03 computes the n=2 minimal polynomial X⁴−10X²+1 (degree 4) and proves it irreducible by hand. This entry is the n=3 step (degree 8); the polynomial degree doubles per added surd, but the brute-force irreducibility argument does not scale, motivating the conditional formulation.
prerequisites: minpoly.dvd / minpoly.eq_of_irreducible_of_monic: divisibility and identification of minimal polynomials

conclusion.summary: Verified with 0 sorries and 0 axioms (no native_decide): the octic X⁸−40X⁶+352X⁴−960X²+576 annihilates √2+√3+√5 and all eight sign-conjugates (conjugates_are_roots), is monic of degree 8, witnesses integrality of α over ℚ, and is divisible by the genuine minimal polynomial. The identity minpoly ℚ α = octic is given conditional on irreducibility (minpoly_eq_of_irreducible). 7 theorems, 162 lines.
conclusion.implications: Provides the explicit degree-8 candidate and its full Galois-conjugate root structure for √2+√3+√5, the unit (k=3) case of the multiquadratic minimal-polynomial family. Combined with a proof of [ℚ(√2+√3+√5):ℚ]=8 (the parent's oq-04), minpoly_eq_of_irreducible would immediately upgrade to an unconditional identity.
openQuestions: Prove irreducibility of X⁸−40X⁶+352X⁴−960X²+576 over ℚ, equivalently [ℚ(√2+√3+√5):ℚ]=8, discharging the hypothesis of minpoly_eq_of_irreducible (this is the parent entry's oq-04).

Prove the eight-fold product identity ∏_{ε∈{±1}³}(X−ε₁√2−ε₂√3−ε₃√5) = X⁸−40X⁶+352X⁴−960X²+576 directly in ℝ[X] (the eight roots are distinct, so it would follow from conjugates_are_roots + monicity once distinctness is formalized).
Generalize to four summands √2+√3+√5+√7 (degree 16) via the same sign-independent isolate-and-square scheme.

crossReferences.description: Parent gallery entry (irrationality of √2+√3+√5). This entry answers its open question oq-03 by computing the explicit degree-8 candidate minimal polynomial and its Galois-conjugate root structure.

Sister entry: the n=2 case, minimal polynomial X⁴−10X²+1 of √2+√3 (degree 4), proved irreducible by a finite rational/quadratic-factor analysis. This entry is the n=3 step (degree 8); the irreducibility argument no longer scales, so the full minpoly identity is left conditional.
Companion open question on the Galois action of (ℤ/2ℤ)³ and [ℚ(√2,√3,√5):ℚ]=8. Proving that degree fact would discharge the irreducibility hypothesis of minpoly_eq_of_irreducible here.

sections.title: Overview and Proof Strategy
sections.summary: Module header: states the candidate octic $X^8-40X^6+352X^4-960X^2+576$, explains how its coefficients arise from the Galois-conjugate product over $\{\pm1\}^3$, lays out the sign-independent isolate-and-square strategy, and is explicit about what is verified (root family, monicity, degree, integrality, divisibility) versus left conditional (irreducibility). Enters the `Sqrt2PlusSqrt3PlusSqrt5IrrationalOQ03` namespace.

sections.title: Part I: The Galois-Conjugate Root Family
sections.summary: Proves `conjugates_are_roots`: for any reals $a,b,c$ with $a^2=2,\,b^2=3,\,c^2=5$, the sum $a+b+c$ is a root of the octic. Establishes $t=bc$ with $t^2=15$, the isolating identity $((a+b+c)^2-6-2t)^2=8(a+b+c)^2$, then a single `linear_combination` collapses to $p(a+b+c)=0$. Because no signs are used, all eight conjugates are covered at once.
sections.mathContext: Sign-independent computation: only $a^2=2,b^2=3,c^2=5$ enter, so $\varepsilon_1\sqrt2+\varepsilon_2\sqrt3+\varepsilon_3\sqrt5$ is a root for every $\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}^3$.

sections.title: Part II: The Candidate Annihilates α
sections.summary: Proves `aeval_minpoly_candidate`: $\sqrt2+\sqrt3+\sqrt5$ is a root of the octic over $\mathbb{Q}$. Reduces `aeval` to the real-number statement via `simp` and `Real.sq_sqrt`, then applies `conjugates_are_roots` with the principal (all-$+$) square roots.
sections.mathContext: $p(\sqrt2+\sqrt3+\sqrt5)=0$ — the explicit annihilating polynomial of the principal conjugate.

sections.title: Part III: Monicity, Degree and Integrality
sections.summary: Establishes `cand_monic` (the octic is monic, via `monicity!`), `cand_natDegree` (degree 8, via `compute_degree!`), and `sqrt_sum_isIntegral` ($\sqrt2+\sqrt3+\sqrt5$ is integral over $\mathbb{Q}$, being a root of this monic polynomial).
sections.mathContext: The octic is monic of degree 8 with $\alpha$ as a root, so $\alpha$ is algebraic of degree $\le 8$ over $\mathbb{Q}$.

sections.title: Part IV: Relation to the Genuine Minimal Polynomial
sections.summary: `minpoly_dvd_cand`: the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ divides the octic (always valid, via `minpoly.dvd`). `minpoly_eq_of_irreducible`: if the octic is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$ then it equals $\mathrm{minpoly}_{\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha)$ — irreducibility (equivalently $[\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2+\sqrt3+\sqrt5):\mathbb{Q}]=8$, the parent's oq-04) is left as an explicit hypothesis, not an axiom.
sections.mathContext: $\mathrm{minpoly}_{\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha)\mid p$ unconditionally; $\mathrm{minpoly}_{\mathbb{Q}}(\alpha)=p$ conditional on irreducibility of $p$.
